Surat "Az-Zalzalah" is Medinan according to Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah, and Meccan according to Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ata' and Jabir. It has nine [[In the margin of al-Shihab: (its verses are nine or eight).]] verses. The scholars said: this surah has great merit, and it contains a great matter. Al-Tirmidhi related from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Idha zulzilat), it is counted for him as half of the Qur'an. Whoever recites ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve﴾ [Al-Kafirun: 1], it is counted for him as a quarter of the Qur'an, and whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ [Al-Ikhlas: 1], it is counted for him as a third of the Qur'an." He said: this is a gharib (rare) hadith, and on this topic there is also a report from Ibn 'Abbas. It is also related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Idha zulzilat four times, it is as if he recited the whole Qur'an." And 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As related: When (Idha zulzilat) was revealed, Abu Bakr wept, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: [If you did not commit errors and sins, and Allah did not forgive you, He would create a people who commit errors and sins, and He would forgive them. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful

﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] shaking﴾ (1). That is, it is moved from its foundation. Thus 'Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas, and he used to say: it is shaken at the first blast. Mujahid also said this, based on the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿On the day when the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 6-7]. Then it is shaken a second time, and it brings forth its dead, and they are the burdens (al-athqal). The verbal noun (al-masdar, the infinitive) is mentioned for emphasis, and then it is attributed to the earth, as when you say: "I will surely give you your gift," meaning my gift to you. This was made good by the agreement of the verse-endings (ru'us al-aya, the final words of verses) that follow it. The reading of the majority is with a kasra on the zay in zilzal, from the verbal noun. Al-Jahdari and 'Isa ibn 'Umar read it with a fatha on it, and it is also a verbal noun, like al-waswas, al-qalqal and al-jarjar [[al-qalqal: from qalqala al-shay' when he moved it. al-jarjar: from jarjara al-ba'ir when he repeated its sound in its throat.]]. It was said: the kasra is the verbal noun, and the fatha is the noun (al-ism, the name).

Abu 'Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: If the dead person is in the belly of the earth, he is a burden to it (ثِقْلٌ لَهَا). And if he is above it, he is a burden upon it (ثِقْلٌ عَلَيْهَا).

Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: "Its burdens" (أَثْقالَها) means its dead, which it brings forth at the second blast (al-nafkha al-thaniya). From this comes the saying that the jinn and mankind are "the two burdens" (al-thaqalan).

Al-Khansa' said:

Far away is Ibn 'Amr from the family of al-Shar-yad, in whom the earth has settled its burdens.

She means: when 'Amr was buried, he became an ornament (hilya) to the people of the graves, because of his nobility and lordship.

Some scholars of knowledge mentioned: The Arabs used to say that if a man was one who shed blood (saffakan lil-dima'), he was a burden upon the back of the earth; when he died, the earth unloaded its burden from its back. It was also said: "Its burdens" (أَثْقالَها) are its treasures (kunuzuha). From this is the hadith: (The earth will expel the pillars of its liver (afladh kabidiha), like pillars (amthal al-ustuwan) of gold and silver...).

[Al-ustuwan: plural of ustuwana, meaning a pillar or column, and the like; it is likened to a pillar because of its size and abundance.]

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 99, verse 3:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And man will say﴾, i.e., the son of Adam, the disbeliever. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "He is al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad." It was also said: He meant every human being who witnesses that at the establishment of the Hour, at the first blast (al-nafkha al-ula), whether believer or disbeliever. This is the view of those who count it (the earthquake) among the signs of the Hour in this world, because they do not all know, at the beginning of its matter, the signs of the Hour, until they become certain of its generality; therefore some of them asked others about it. And according to the view of those who said that the intended "man" is the disbelievers specifically, he made it the quaking of the Resurrection, because the believer acknowledges it, so he does not ask about it, while the disbeliever denies it, so he asks about it. And the meaning of ﴿What is the matter with it?﴾ is: what is the matter with it, that it has been shaken. It was also said: what is the matter with it, that it has brought forth its burdens; and this is an expression of wonder, meaning: for what reason has it been shaken? It is also possible that God revives the dead after the occurrence of the first blast, then the earth moves and brings forth the dead, and they have seen the quaking and the splitting of the earth open to the dead as living beings, so they say, from terror: "What is the matter with it?"

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 99, verse 4–6:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾. "On that Day" (yawma'idhin) is in the accusative, governed by His saying: "When the earth is shaken" (idha zulzilat). It was also said that it is governed by His saying "it will report its news," meaning: the earth will inform, on that Day, of what good or evil was done upon it. Then it was said: this is part of the speech of Allah, may He be exalted. And it was said: it is part of the speech of the human being, meaning the human being says, in wonder, "What is wrong with it, that it reports its news?"

In at-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse, ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾, and said: "Do you know what its news is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Its news is that it will bear witness against every male and female servant for what they did upon its back: it will say, 'He did such-and-such on such-and-such a day.' That is its news." He said: This is a hasan sahih hadith.

Al-Mawardi said: Regarding His saying, ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾, there are three opinions:

First: it reports its news of the deeds of the servants upon its back. This was said by Abu Hurayra, and he narrated it as a marfu' report. This is the view of those who hold that it refers to the quake of the Resurrection.

Second: it reports its news of what it brought forth of its burdens. This was said by Yahya ibn Sallam. This is the view of those who hold that it refers to the quake of the portents of the Hour. I say: There is a hadith with this meaning narrated by Ibn Mas'ud from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "When a servant's term is in a land, or need keeps him attached to it, until he reaches the furthest point of his trace, Allah takes him; then on the Day of Resurrection the earth will say: 'My Lord, this is what You entrusted to me.'" Ibn Majah recorded it in his Sunan. It has been mentioned previously [see vol. 14, p. 83].

Third: it will report of the establishment of the Hour when the human being says, "What is wrong with it?" This was said by Ibn Mas'ud. It will inform that the affair of the world has ended and the affair of the Hereafter has come. So that will be its answer to them when they ask, a threat to the disbeliever and a warning to the believer. Regarding its reporting of its news there are three opinions: First: Allah, may He be exalted, will turn it into a speaking living creature, and it will speak of that. Second: Allah, may He be exalted, will create speech in it. Third: there will come from it a manifestation that takes the place of speech. Al-Tabari said: It makes clear its news by its shaking, its quaking, and the bringing forth of the dead.

﴿For your Lord has inspired it﴾: meaning it reports its news by the inspiration of Allah to it, that is, into it. The Arabs place the lam of attribution in the position of "ila" (to). Al-'Ajjaj, describing the earth, said:

"He inspired it to settle, so it settled, and fastened it with the firm, lofty mountains."

This is the view of Abu 'Ubayda: "awha laha" means "awha ilayha" (inspired to it). It was also said: "awha laha" means "amarahā" (commanded it), as said by Mujahid. Al-Suddi said: "awha laha" means "qala laha" (said to it), and he said: "sakhkharaha" (subjected it). It was also said: the meaning is: on the Day when the quake occurs and the earth brings forth its burdens, the earth will report its news, what was upon it of obedience and disobedience, and what was done upon its back of good and evil. This was related from al-Thawri and others.

﴿On that Day mankind will issue forth in scattered groups﴾: meaning in separate groups, plural of "shatt." It was said: they will depart from the place of reckoning; one group takes the direction of the right toward Paradise, and another group takes the direction of the left toward the Fire, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿On that Day they will be divided﴾ [al-Rum: 14], ﴿On that Day they will be separated﴾ [al-Rum: 43]. It was also said: they will return from the reckoning after finishing the reckoning. "Ashtatan" means groups upon groups.

﴿That they may be shown their deeds﴾: meaning the reward of their deeds. This is like what was related from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "There is no one on the Day of Resurrection except that he blames himself: if he was a doer of good, he says, 'Why did I not increase my good?' and if he was otherwise, he says, 'Why did I not refrain from sins?'" This occurs at the moment of witnessing the reward and the punishment. Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "ashtatan" means scattered according to their deeds: the people of faith are separate, and the people of each religion are separate. It was also said: this issuing forth happens only at the resurrection: they will issue forth in scattered groups from the graves, and they will be brought to the place of reckoning, so that they may be shown their deeds in their books, or that they may be shown the recompense of their deeds. It is as if they had come to the graves, were buried in them, and then departed from them. "Al-warid" is the one who comes, and "al-sadir" is the one who turns away. "Ashtatan" means they will be raised from the regions of the earth. According to the first opinion, there is an inversion of order in it; its meaning is: "She will report her news, because your Lord has inspired her, that they may be shown their deeds." It was objected: His saying "On that Day mankind will issue forth in scattered groups, separated from the place of reckoning."

The reading of the common people is "liyurau" with a dammah on the ya', meaning that Allah will show them their deeds. Al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, Qatada, al-A'raj, Nasr ibn 'Asim and Talha read it with a fatha on the ya', and this was related from the Prophet (ﷺ).

**Third issue:** Qur'an 99:7–8 (al-Qurtubi)

There are three issues in this verse.

**The first issue:** God's words, ﴿Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾. Ibn 'Abbas used to say: whoever among the disbelievers does an atom's weight of good will see it in this world, and will not be rewarded for it in the Hereafter. Whoever does an atom's weight of evil will be punished for it in the Hereafter, along with the punishment for shirk. Whoever among the believers does an atom's weight of evil will see it in this world, and will not be punished for it in the Hereafter if he dies, and it will be overlooked. If he does an atom's weight of good, it will be accepted from him and multiplied for him in the Hereafter.

Some hadith say: "The *dharrah* (atom, or mote) has no weight." This is a parable God gave: that He does not overlook any of the deeds of the children of Adam, small or great. It is like God's words: ﴿Indeed, God does not wrong anyone the weight of an atom﴾ [An-Nisa larger: 40]. The discussion of *dharr* was already given there, and that it has no weight.

Some lexicographers mention that *dharr* is when a man strikes the ground with his hand; whatever dust clings to it is *dharr*. Ibn 'Abbas likewise said: when you place your hand on the ground and lift it, each particle of dust that adheres to it is a *dharrah*.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: ﴿whoever does an atom's weight of good﴾ (done by a disbeliever) ﴿will see its reward﴾ in this world, in his self, his wealth, his family and his children, until he leaves this world with no good with God. And ﴿whoever does an atom's weight of evil﴾ (done by a believer) ﴿will see its punishment﴾ in this world, in his self, his wealth, his children and his family, until he leaves this world with no evil with God.

The evidence for this is what the reliable scholars narrated from the hadith of Anas: this verse was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) while Abu Bakr was eating. He stopped and said: "O Messenger of God, will we see what we have done of good and evil?" He said: "What you see of what you dislike is the atoms' weights of evil, and what is stored up for you are the atoms' weights of good, until you receive them on the Day of Resurrection."

Abu Idris said: its confirmation in the Book of God is: ﴿Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [Ash-Shura: 30].

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning two men, because when God revealed ﴿and they give food, in spite of their love for it﴾ [Al-Insan: 8], one of them, when a beggar came to him, would consider it too much to give him a date, a morsel, or a walnut (*jawzah*, a single walnut, a Persian loanword in Arabic). The other would treat small sins lightly, such as a lie, backbiting, or a glance, saying: "God only threatened the Fire for the major sins." So the verse was revealed, encouraging them to give even a little good, for it is about to increase, and warning them against even a small sin, for it is about to grow. Sa'id ibn Jubayr also said this. A small sin in the eyes of its doer on the Day of Resurrection is greater than mountains, and all his good deeds are less in his eyes than anything.

**The second issue:** The common reading is *yarahu* (يَرَهُ) with a fatha on the *ya'* in both places. Al-Jahdari, al-Sulami, 'Isa ibn 'Umar and Aban from 'Asim read *yurahu* (يُرَهُ) with a damma on the *ya'*, meaning God shows it to him. The first reading is preferred, because of God's words: ﴿on the Day when every soul will find what it has done of good present﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 30], and so on.

Hisham read the *ha'* with sukun (silent) in both places. Likewise al-Kisa'i transmitted it from Abu Bakr, Abu Haywa and al-Mughirah. Ya'qub, al-Zuhri, al-Jahdari and Shayba used *ikhtilas* (a shortened, quick vowel). The rest pronounced it fully.

It is said that *yarahu* means he will see its reward, because what he did has passed and ceased to exist, so it is not seen. They recited:

*Indeed, whoever transgresses and earns sin,*
*the weight of an atom, he will see it.*

*He is repaid for his deed with evil, evil,*
*and for a good deed, good as well.*

*Thus is the saying of my Lord, blessed is He,*
*in "When the earth is shaken" and His praise is exalted.*

**The third issue:** Ibn Mas'ud said: this is the most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an, and he spoke truly. The scholars agreed on the generality of this verse, both those who hold that it is general and those who do not.

Ka'b al-Ahbar narrated that he said: God revealed to Muhammad two verses that encompass what is in the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and the scrolls: ﴿whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾, and ﴿whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾.

Shaykh Abu Madyan said concerning God's words ﴿whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾: "In the present state, before the final outcome."

The Prophet (ﷺ) used to call this verse "the comprehensive, unique verse," as in the Sahih, when he was asked about donkeys and remained silent about mules. The answer regarding both is the same, because mules and donkeys have neither charging nor retreating in them. When the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned the lasting reward and continuous recompense in horses, the questioner asked about donkeys, because at that time they did not have mules, and no mule had entered the Hijaz except the Prophet's mule, "al-Duldul," which al-Muqawqis had given him. So he gave him a ruling about donkeys based on the generality of the verse, and that there are many atoms' weights in a donkey. This was said by Ibn al-'Arabi.

In the Muwatta: a poor man asked 'A'isha, the Mother of the Believers, for food while she had grapes before her. She said to a person: "Take a single grape and give it to him." He kept looking at it in wonder, and she said: "Are you surprised? How many atoms' weights do you see in this single grape?"

It is narrated from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas that he gave away two dates in charity, and the beggar closed his hand. He said to the beggar: "Will God accept from us the weights of atoms? There are many atoms' weights in two dates."

Al-Mutallib ibn Hantab narrated that a Bedouin heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite it, and said: "O Messenger of God, an atom's weight?" He said: "Yes." The Bedouin said: "Woe to me!" several times, then he got up while still saying it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Faith has entered the heart of the Bedouin."

Al-Hasan said: Sa'sa'ah, the paternal uncle of al-Farazdaq, came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and when he heard ﴿whoever does an atom's weight﴾ and the verses that follow, he said: "I do not care if I hear nothing else of the Qur'an; it is enough for me, for the admonition has ended." Al-Tha'labi mentioned it.

The wording of al-Mawardi is: it is narrated that Sa'sa'ah ibn Najiyah, the grandfather of al-Farazdaq, came to the Prophet (ﷺ) asking him to recite. He recited this verse to him, and Sa'sa'ah said: "Enough, enough. If I do an atom's weight of evil, I will see it."

Ma'mar narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Teach me from what God has taught you." He handed him over to a man to teach him, and he taught him *Idha zulzilat* up to ﴿whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾. The man said: "Enough." The Prophet (ﷺ) was informed and said: "Leave him, for he has understood."

It is related that a Bedouin delayed "will see it" (in recitation), and it was said to him: "You have put forward and delayed." He said:

*Take the belly of Harsha or its back,*
*for both sides of Harsha lead to the same road.*

**Third issue:** Qur'an 99:7–8 (al-Qurtubi)

There are three issues in this verse.

**The first issue:** God's words, ﴿Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾. Ibn 'Abbas used to say: whoever among the disbelievers does an atom's weight of good will see it in this world, and will not be rewarded for it in the Hereafter. Whoever does an atom's weight of evil will be punished for it in the Hereafter, along with the punishment for shirk. Whoever among the believers does an atom's weight of evil will see it in this world, and will not be punished for it in the Hereafter if he dies, and it will be overlooked. If he does an atom's weight of good, it will be accepted from him and multiplied for him in the Hereafter.

Some hadith say: "The *dharrah* (atom, or mote) has no weight." This is a parable God gave: that He does not overlook any of the deeds of the children of Adam, small or great. It is like God's words: ﴿Indeed, God does not wrong anyone the weight of an atom﴾ [An-Nisa larger: 40]. The discussion of *dharr* was already given there, and that it has no weight.

Some lexicographers mention that *dharr* is when a man strikes the ground with his hand; whatever dust clings to it is *dharr*. Ibn 'Abbas likewise said: when you place your hand on the ground and lift it, each particle of dust that adheres to it is a *dharrah*.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: ﴿whoever does an atom's weight of good﴾ (done by a disbeliever) ﴿will see its reward﴾ in this world, in his self, his wealth, his family and his children, until he leaves this world with no good with God. And ﴿whoever does an atom's weight of evil﴾ (done by a believer) ﴿will see its punishment﴾ in this world, in his self, his wealth, his children and his family, until he leaves this world with no evil with God.

The evidence for this is what the reliable scholars narrated from the hadith of Anas: this verse was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) while Abu Bakr was eating. He stopped and said: "O Messenger of God, will we see what we have done of good and evil?" He said: "What you see of what you dislike is the atoms' weights of evil, and what is stored up for you are the atoms' weights of good, until you receive them on the Day of Resurrection."

Abu Idris said: its confirmation in the Book of God is: ﴿Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [Ash-Shura: 30].

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning two men, because when God revealed ﴿and they give food, in spite of their love for it﴾ [Al-Insan: 8], one of them, when a beggar came to him, would consider it too much to give him a date, a morsel, or a walnut (*jawzah*, a single walnut, a Persian loanword in Arabic). The other would treat small sins lightly, such as a lie, backbiting, or a glance, saying: "God only threatened the Fire for the major sins." So the verse was revealed, encouraging them to give even a little good, for it is about to increase, and warning them against even a small sin, for it is about to grow. Sa'id ibn Jubayr also said this. A small sin in the eyes of its doer on the Day of Resurrection is greater than mountains, and all his good deeds are less in his eyes than anything.

**The second issue:** The common reading is *yarahu* (يَرَهُ) with a fatha on the *ya'* in both places. Al-Jahdari, al-Sulami, 'Isa ibn 'Umar and Aban from 'Asim read *yurahu* (يُرَهُ) with a damma on the *ya'*, meaning God shows it to him. The first reading is preferred, because of God's words: ﴿on the Day when every soul will find what it has done of good present﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 30], and so on.

Hisham read the *ha'* with sukun (silent) in both places. Likewise al-Kisa'i transmitted it from Abu Bakr, Abu Haywa and al-Mughirah. Ya'qub, al-Zuhri, al-Jahdari and Shayba used *ikhtilas* (a shortened, quick vowel). The rest pronounced it fully.

It is said that *yarahu* means he will see its reward, because what he did has passed and ceased to exist, so it is not seen. They recited:

*Indeed, whoever transgresses and earns sin,*
*the weight of an atom, he will see it.*

*He is repaid for his deed with evil, evil,*
*and for a good deed, good as well.*

*Thus is the saying of my Lord, blessed is He,*
*in "When the earth is shaken" and His praise is exalted.*
